topic: SDP vs LDP vs DNP Night Interruption, Pr/Pfr Interconversions, Florigen (FT), & FLC Epigenetics

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 9.1 Photoperiodism (Garner & Allard, 1920)
Photoperiodism is the physiological response to the relative lengths of light and dark periods regulating flowering.
- **Short-Day Plants (SDP)**: Require night length exceeding critical duration (*Tobacco, Soybean, Cocklebur*). A brief flash of red light during the night **inhibits** flowering.
- **Long-Day Plants (LDP)**: Require light exceeding critical duration (*Henbane, Wheat, Radish*). A red flash during night **promotes** flowering.
- **Day-Neutral Plants (DNP)**: Flowering is independent of photoperiod (*Tomato, Sunflower, Cucumber, Maize*).

### 9.2 Phytochrome Photoreceptor & Florigen
- **Phytochrome**: Blue-green chromoprotein in leaves. Exists as $\text{P}_r$ (absorbs $660\text{ nm}$, inactive) and $\text{P}_{fr}$ (absorbs $730\text{ nm}$, biologically active).
- **Florigen**: Systemic flowering signal (FT protein) synthesized in leaves under inductive photoperiods and transported via phloem to the shoot apex.

### 9.3 Vernalization (Cold Temperature Induction)
- Requirement for low temperature ($1\text{--}10^\circ\text{C}$) to induce flowering in winter annuals (*Wheat, Barley*) and biennials (*Cabbage, Sugarbeet*).
- **Perception Site**: Actively dividing meristematic cells (shoot apical meristem or embryo).
- **Epigenetic Mechanism**: Cold exposure epigenetically silences the floral repressor gene *FLC* (*Flowering Locus C*).
